solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's pointlessly subject to being extravagant

indicators.note: without a point: one compass point, the letter for south, is dropped from the word

parts.note: slavish means servile, wholly subject to another

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is wastefully extravagant for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointlessly' tells you to lose a compass point, here S, from SLAVISH. 'It's' and 'being' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish and extravagant are synonyms, both describing spending or giving with great abundance.

clue.text: Without vigour of late?

definitions.meaning: late can mean dead, so of the late is without life

explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless means dull and spiritless, and literally dead, as the late are.

clue.text: A fiver rise for the linesman

indicators.note: assumed signal for rearranging the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone pays a touch-judge a five-pound raise.
explanation.definitionFit: A versifier writes lines of verse, so is cryptically a man of lines.

clue.text: Pass around the mugs

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into another order

explanation.surface: Hand the drinking cups round.
explanation.definitionFit: Saps are gullible fools, the same sense as mugs.

clue.text: Pirates on land and in ships

indicators.note: the word and is placed inside the vessels named next

parts.note: brigs are two-masted sailing ships
taken as written

explanation.surface: Robbers who work both ashore and aboard ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigands are bandits who rob travellers, the land-based counterpart of seafaring raiders.

clue.text: Gentleman burglar held to raise money

definitions.meaning: A. J. ..., the cricketing gentleman thief in E. W. Hornung's stories
lotteries run with prizes to raise funds for a cause

explanation.definitionFit: Raffles is the fictional gentleman thief, and raffles are prize draws held to raise funds.

clue.text: Craftsmen do in G & S role perhaps

indicators.note: signals that the letters might be ordered differently

explanation.surface: Craftsmen perform a Gilbert and Sullivan part.
explanation.walkthrough: G & S is Gilbert and Sullivan, whose operetta The Gondoliers fits the surface. Craftsmen are men who work boats, or craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Gondoliers are men who steer craft, gondolas in Venice, so craft-men.

clue.text: Almost terrified, initially, of the dark

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Being nearly terrified of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness between dusk and dawn.

clue.text: Sadly, elevated railway provides payment only for non-manual workers

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted up so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: alas is a cry meaning sadly

explanation.surface: An overhead railway pays only its office staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated railway' looks like one thing, an overhead line, but 'elevated' turns ALAS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is fixed pay usually given to office or professional staff, wage-earners being paid weekly.

clue.text: Contending successfully with the top course

definitions.meaning: managing or dealing well with a difficulty
the top layer of masonry on a wall

explanation.definitionFit: Coping means managing a difficulty, and coping is the capping course on a wall.

clue.text: Not to be made light of

definitions.text: Not to be made light of

parts.words: Not to be made light of
parts.note: reads like 'not to be taken lightly', but means something that cannot be set alight

explanation.definitionFit: A fireproof material cannot be lit, so it will never be 'made light' in the sense of set burning.

clue.text: He'll give support in return

indicators.note: read the letters backwards, as if coming back

parts.note: a leg is a limb or post that supports something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who will offer help when his turn comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In return' turns LEGIN round. The definition is just 'He', a man's name standing for any man.
explanation.definitionFit: A first name for a man, so a fair example of the pronoun he.

clue.text: Rail put about animal's den

indicators.note: the letters of the word are turned and moved around, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Fencing rails are set round the den of a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's lair is the den or hiding place where it lives.

clue.text: One who sticks at his job and mails his account?

definitions.text: One who sticks at his job
definitions.meaning: someone who pastes up posters, literally sticking things as work
read whimsically, one who posts the bill he is owed

explanation.definitionFit: A billposter pastes posters on walls, and split in two it suggests one who posts a bill.

clue.text: Groundless gossip that there's unemployment?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, a rumour about people being idle

explanation.definitionFit: An idle rumour is baseless hearsay, and could whimsically be talk about joblessness.

clue.text: Dishing out for a party

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Serving food at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is informal slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Recalling students by mistake

indicators.note: calling back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pupils are students at a school

explanation.surface: A school summons pupils back in error.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is an informal term for a careless mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Marriage, with something to raise the standard

parts.note: a union is a marriage
a jack is a device to lift a car

explanation.surface: A wedding brings something to improve standards.
explanation.walkthrough: A standard here is a flag, the Union Jack being the flag of the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the national flag of Britain.

clue.text: Masters taking PE?

definitions.meaning: captains of ships are their masters
people skipping in a physical education class

explanation.definitionFit: Skippers are ship captains, or masters, and also people who skip, as in a gym class.

clue.text: Full of zeal for a new trend

indicators.note: the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Being enthusiastic about the latest fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent describes someone passionate and fervent, eager in pursuit of something.

clue.text: Cultivation that's up to date

parts.note: till means until, up to a time
an age is a period, a date in history

explanation.surface: Farming that is modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the tilling of land, cultivating the soil for crops.

clue.text: Richard admits blunder with crane

indicators.note: lets in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Dick is the familiar short form of the name Richard
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Richard owns up to a mistake involving a crane.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is a kind of crane for lifting heavy loads, as on docks or oil rigs.

clue.text: Corrupt passage

explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to make impure, and a defile is a narrow pass between hills.

clue.text: Revised diet arranged with Edward

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward has rearranged his eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited means corrected or revised, as text is after editing.

clue.text: Exclude underworld leader with pass

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld, also called Pluto
to qualify is to pass a test or meet a standard

explanation.surface: A gang boss with a pass is barred from entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld leader' hints at a crime boss but points to the classical god Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: To disqualify someone is to rule them out or bar them from a contest.

clue.text: Plays guitar with spirit on the street

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece is placed beneath the other

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A busker plays guitar on the street fuelled by drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum is to sweep the fingers across guitar strings.

clue.text: Break a spell

explanation.definitionFit: Snap means to break cleanly, and also a brief spell of weather, as in a cold snap.

clue.text: I've turned left — it's not right

indicators.note: the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone changes political side, which is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' and 'right' look like a pair of directions, but 'not right' is moral wrongness.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is what is morally wrong, the opposite of right conduct.

clue.text: Elephant's tail, something like the trunk

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: 'or so' means approximately, something like it

explanation.surface: An elephant's tail looks a bit like its trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The elephant suggests its trunk literally, but the trunk here is the human body's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human trunk, the body without head or limbs.

clue.text: A novice gets priest at end of service to moderate

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
Levi, head of the Levites, the priestly tribe of Israel

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A trainee is given a priest at the end of a church service to calm things.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate is to ease or lessen, to make something less severe.

clue.text: Violently murdered having refused consent

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about violently into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone killed after saying no.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to object, so having demurred means having raised objections and declined.

clue.text: They are lucky most anchors have more than one

definitions.text: most anchors have more than one
definitions.meaning: the flat barbed blades on an anchor's arms

explanation.definitionFit: Flukes are lucky strokes of chance, and also the pointed blades on the arms of an anchor.
